symptoms_only_example.headline: Worth getting tested
symptoms_only_example.summary: Your answers suggest a confidential test is worthwhile. Most of what causes these symptoms is common and treatable, and the test itself takes minutes.
reasons: No visible skin change was reported, so no photo was analysed; this assessment is based on your answers alone.
Symptoms without a visible change still need assessment: discharge, pain when urinating, pain or burning.
Discharge or pain on urination are the classic signs of chlamydia, gonorrhoea or a urinary infection, all diagnosed by a simple urine or swab test.
Pain or burning without a visible change can come from inflammation, infection or injury and is worth examining.
actions: Book a confidential sexual-health check within the next one to two weeks.
Avoid sexual contact until you have been tested, or use condoms consistently.
A urine sample and a swab or blood test are usually all that is needed.
If the contact was within the last 72 hours, contact a clinic or emergency department today and ask about PEP (HIV post-exposure prophylaxis); it works best the sooner it is started.
testing: chlamydia and gonorrhoea NAAT (urine or swab)
routine STI screen (HIV, syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea)
notes: Tests have window periods: chlamydia and gonorrhoea from about 2 weeks after contact, HIV about 45 days for a 4th-generation test (3 months to be certain), syphilis 6 to 12 weeks. A clinic will tell you when to test and whether to re-test.
Because nothing is visible, a photo would not add anything here. A test is the right next step, and it is quick: usually a urine sample, a swab or a small blood draw.

differential: thrush (candida), which is not usually sexually transmitted
